title: Chapter 37 — Upupiformes
description: A small order of just three closely related hoopoe species, characterised by bold black-and-white barred wings, cinnamon plumage, and a dramatic fan-shaped erectile crest. Found across Africa, Europe, and Asia.

children.name: Upupa
children.description: One of the most striking birds of the Western Palearctic — salmon-pink with bold black-and-white barred wings and a dramatic fan-shaped crest raised in alarm or display. The oop-oop-oop call carries far over open Swedish landscapes. An irregular visitor to the south, with occasional breeding records in warm years.

children.name: Upupa epops
children.description: The Eurasian hoopoe or common hoopoe is the most widespread species of the genus Upupa. It is a distinctive cinnamon coloured bird with black and white wings, a tall erectile crest, a broad white band across a black tail, and a long narrow downcurved bill. Its call is a soft "oop-oop-oop".

children.name: Upupa africana
children.description: The Eurasian hoopoe or common hoopoe (Upupa epops) is the most widespread species of the genus Upupa.

children.name: Upupa marginata
children.description: The Madagascar hoopoe (Upupa marginata) is a species of hoopoe in the family Upupidae.
